findings.title: Cache key uses process-randomized hash(), invalidation won't work across processes
findings.body: The cache key embeds Python's `hash()` of a tuple of project IDs. Tuples of ints hash deterministically, so key collisions are possible but rare. The bigger problem is the invalidation design: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` must be called with exactly the same project set that was queried. Nothing in this PR calls it when the allowlist option changes. As a result, allowlist changes take up to 60s to apply for every project combination, which contradicts the 'always latest configuration' note at line 50. The tests that patch `options` can also be affected by stale cache entries left from earlier tests.

findings.title: Substring check for event.type:error matches negated queries
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` does a substring search for `event.type:error`. A query like `!event.type:error` or `event.type:error_foo` also matches. Negated queries (e.g. `!event.type:error`, which selects transactions) would get the `sum(sample_weight)` transform. That produces wrong counts, or a query failure on the transactions storage.

findings.title: Upsampling decision uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset/split query
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is passed the outer `dataset` and reads the query from `request.GET`. It ignores the `scoped_dataset` and `query` actually being executed. In the dashboard split paths, the discover sub-queries for errors-only and transactions-only can therefore get an inconsistent decision. For example, the transactions-only query can be upsampled when the original request contained `event.type:error`.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight without fallback
findings.body: `sum(sample_weight)` assumes every event has `sample_weight`. Events ingested before the feature, or without a client sample rate, will have null weight and be dropped from the count. Using something like `ifNull(sample_weight, 1)` would avoid undercounting errors.

findings.title: Accidental submodule commit added
findings.body: A `sentry-repo` gitlink pointing at the base commit was added to the repository. This looks accidental and will break clones and CI that try to resolve the submodule.

findings.title: Linear allowlist membership per project
findings.body: `project_id in allowlist` scans the list once for each project, which is O(n*m). Converting the allowlist to a set first would make each lookup constant time.
